A 66-year-old male with a history of congestive heart disease (ejection fraction 40%) is brought to the
emergency department due to severe dyspnea and orthopnea lasting 6 hours. He is confused upon
arrival. His vital signs include a blood pressure of 175/113 mm Hg, pulse of 137/min, respirations of
45/min, and temperature of 36.2°C (97.2°F). Physical examination reveals crackles at both lung bases
and bilateral pitting edema from the mid-tibia to the ankle. The patient is intubated and admitted to the
intensive care unit for mechanical ventilation and treatment, including intravenous morphine, diuretics,
and nitroglycerin. Which of the following measures is most effective in reducing the risk of a nosocomial
infection in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Prioritizing condom catheter over indwelling cather (B)
Early removal of all invasive devices (C) Daily oropharynx decontamination with antiseptic agent (D)
Use of silver-coated endotracheal tubes (E) Regular rotation of IV insertion sites (F) Daily urinary
catheter irrigation with antimicrobial agent (G) Prophylactic systemic antibiotics (H) Suprapubic
catheter insertion (I) Implementation of closed suction systems (J) Strict hand hygiene protocol
implementation
 A. Strict hand hygiene protocol implementation
